- Frame upright (rectangle): fills vertically (top-to-bottom)
- Frame rotated (diamond): fills diagonally
I need to understand the target better. The top-left panel shows white on top, purple on bottom as rectangles. So the target is a rectangular split.
Let me go back to the rectangular frame and think about this differently. Maybe I need to:
1. Reset to the initial state somehow
2. Or use a different approach
Actually, wait. Let me re-read the initial state. The initial state had:
- Purple in frame
- Purple strip below (5 rows)
- White strip below that (5 rows)
And the target (top-left) shows white on top, purple on bottom.
So the goal is to make the area below the frame match the top-left pattern: white on top, purple on bottom.
Currently after my actions, the state is messed up with a diamond fill. Let me reset by rotating back to rectangle and then figuring out the right sequence.
Actually, maybe the approach is:
1. Rotate frame to rectangle (RIGHT)
2. Select white, SPACE to fill all white
3. Select purple, SPACE to fill bottom half purple
But that gives purple on top, white on bottom. Unless... the fill direction depends on which color is selected. Let me think again.
When I select white and SPACE, white expands downward. When I select purple and SPACE, purple expands downward. So the color that's selected is the one that grows.
To get white on top and purple on bottom:
1. First fill everything with purple (select purple, SPACE until all purple)
2. Then fill with white from top (select white, SPACE until 5 rows white)
Wait, but SPACE always fills from the frame downward. If I fill all purple first, then select white and SPACE, white would grow from the top pushing purple down. That would give white on top, purple on bottom!
Let me try this.
